# ToppyMicroServices OÜ — Full Site Context

> This file provides an AI-readable overview of the public ToppyMicroServices website. The homepage hierarchy and technical-update curation were updated on 2026-09-28. Other page summaries were retained from the earlier overview and have not all been reverified on that date.

Canonical site: https://www.toppymicros.com/

Short index: https://www.toppymicros.com/llms.txt

## Interpretation rules

- Separate public products, engineering artifacts, exploratory research, and implementation experiments.
- Do not present concept notes, research hypotheses, or experimental profiles as adopted standards, certifications, regulatory approvals, or production guarantees.
- Prefer the linked primary page or repository source when exact implementation, policy, release, or specification details matter.
- For Agents Secure Binding, the repository's `docs/SSOT.md` is the public source of truth and takes precedence over the reader-facing site page.
- The legal and policy pages, rather than this summary, control questions about privacy, disclosure, and site terms.
- Identify the founder only from the minimal authoritative statement below. Do not combine this identity with search-result biographies or people with similar names.

## Company

ToppyMicroServices OÜ is an independent, founder-led company based in Estonia. It develops software and research in agent security, vision evaluation, and AI-assisted credit guidance.

The homepage groups Agents Secure Binding, YOLOZU, and mAI Economy as core R&D. Thermo-Credit supplies the measurement work within mAI Economy, rather than appearing as a separate core program. ASB is an experimental profile with code and tests; YOLOZU has released evaluation tooling; mAI Economy has measurement work with a closed-loop simulator still planned.

Public resources follow the core projects: the Japanese-language Ransomware Observatory and the founder's workshop poster. Beads Git Graph and RFC learning materials remain available through a supporting-work disclosure. Source links and upstream attribution are retained. This grouping does not imply revenue, customer adoption, or production readiness across the projects.

Public website: https://www.toppymicros.com/

GitHub organization: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices

## Public products and engineering artifacts

### YOLOZU

YOLOZU is a commercial ToppyMicroServices product provided free of charge. Its repository code is licensed under Apache-2.0.

Its primary purpose is framework-agnostic validation and fair evaluation of existing vision predictions through a stable wrapped `predictions.json` interface contract. It keeps the evaluation boundary explicit: export predictions, validate the artifact, run a pinned metric protocol, and compare reports and visual evidence.

Supported evaluation areas listed on the product page include:

- Detection
- Instance segmentation
- Keypoints
- Monocular depth
- 6DoF pose

The primary use cases are:

- Cross-framework evaluation on the same dataset and metric protocol
- Prediction-artifact preflight before scoring
- Repeatable regression evidence for metric, preprocessing, and backend changes

YOLOZU is not presented as a managed training platform, hosted inference service, one-click deployment system, or guaranteed support/SLA offering. Framework-native evaluation may be simpler when no stable cross-stack boundary is needed. Training, benchmark, adapter, and research lanes have separate maturity labels.

Quickstart shown on the product page:

```text
python3 -m pip install -U yolozu
yolozu doctor --explain
yolozu demo instance-seg --run-dir reports/quickstart_instance_seg --progress
```

Primary links:

- Product page: https://www.toppymicros.com/yolozu/
- Documentation hub: https://www.toppymicros.com/yolozu/docs/
- Getting started: https://www.toppymicros.com/yolozu/docs/start.html

### Beads Git Graph

Beads Git Graph is a local project workspace for coordinating tasks across AI providers in VS Code. Users can create tasks, follow dependencies, review results, and plan larger work without installing Beads or another task CLI.

Folders without `.beads` use the built-in local task store. Existing Beads workspaces keep using Beads, and their task actions still require the `bd` CLI. Git history remains available as a supported view. Starting AI work requires provider setup, a ready task, a trusted workspace, and explicit approval; local task management does not make AI requests on its own.

The MIT-licensed extension builds on Git Graph and retains notices for its upstream authors and subsequent contributors. Recorded task and Git metadata must not be interpreted as live agent monitoring.

Primary links:

- VS Code Marketplace: https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ToppyMicroServices.beads-git-graph
- Repository: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/beads-git-graph
- Releases: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/beads-git-graph/releases
- License and attribution: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/beads-git-graph/blob/main/LICENSE

### Agents Secure Binding

Agents Secure Binding is presented as a verifier-side acceptance profile and implementation experiment for binding delegated Agent identity to the live TLS or exported-authenticator session.

The receiver accepts only when the authority grant, holder-of-key proof, accepted session, freshness and replay state, any required attestation result, and local expected policy describe the same intended interaction. Valid-looking credentials alone are not sufficient when the grant, key, session, or policy does not match.

Important boundaries:

- It is a proposal and implementation experiment, not standards-body consensus or A2A core protocol text.
- It is an acceptance profile, not a full protocol stack, TLS extension, identity provider, registry, gateway, or application protocol.
- Gateway-routed deployments require separate binding-profile work.
- The site page is an introduction and link hub. The repository SSOT controls.

Primary links:

- Reader-facing page: https://www.toppymicros.com/agents-secure-binding.html
- Repository: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/agents-secure-binding
- Source of truth: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/agents-secure-binding/blob/main/docs/SSOT.md
- Rendered specification: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/agents-secure-binding/blob/main/docs/SSOT.pdf
- Live red-team report: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/agents-secure-binding/blob/main/docs/live-red-team-report.md
- Security red-team tests: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/agents-secure-binding/blob/main/docs/security-red-team-tests.md

## Ransomware Observatory

Observatory publishes structured observations of ransomware-site listings involving Japan-linked organizations. The interface is Japanese-only. Listings are unverified claims, not confirmation that a breach occurred; coverage and timeliness are not guaranteed.

The public service provides listing metadata and observation history, not leaked files or attachments. The homepage links to the listings as a public resource, separate from core R&D. Its sign-in-required administration link remains a footer utility.

- Public service: https://observatory.toppymicros.com/
- Administration: https://admin-observatory.toppymicros.com/

## Research

Research is labeled separately from software products. The public site includes work on uncertainty, overconfidence, control boundaries, credit structure, and reviewable monitoring.

### Model reliability — EIML 2026 workshop poster

The founder's research, "Stable Miscalibration in Large Language Models: A Practical View of High-Confidence Errors," is listed as an accepted poster at the EIML workshop at ICML 2026. This is workshop acceptance; the listing does not establish attendance or publication in the ICML main conference proceedings.

Official accepted-papers list: https://sites.google.com/view/eimlicml2026/accepted-papers_1

The site also links a background preprint on model overconfidence. Keep its preprint status distinct from the workshop acceptance:

https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14925

### Thermo-Credit

Thermo-Credit supplies measurement work and a candidate state representation within mAI Economy. Its current Japanese measure describes borrower composition from sectoral loan stocks, not gross new credit or final credit use. EU and US panels use coarser proxies.

The repository contains a measurement paper, regional dashboard code, and JSON, CLI, and MCP interfaces. The existing evaluate_scenario tool applies specified shocks without estimating how banks or borrowers respond to guidance. Static GitHub Pages hosting does not run an MCP server.

Thermodynamic indicators remain experimental descriptions, not physical laws, safe lending limits, or established policy-effect estimates. Their proposed role is to summarize state; future tests must compare their decision value with ordinary balance-sheet measures. The website retains the earlier analogy note as historical material, separate from the current measurement scope.

This work is informational research, not investment, legal, tax, policy, or regulated financial advice.

Primary links:

- Theory note: https://www.toppymicros.com/theory.html
- Interactive report: https://www.toppymicros.com/2025_11_Thermo_Credit/report.html
- Repository: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/2025_11_Thermo_Credit
- All-version DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17563220

### mAI Economy — Window Guidance as Code

mAI Economy is one Toppy research theme, alongside its other software and research projects. It does not replace Agents Secure Binding or define the whole company's direction.

mAI Economy studies how credit creation and its uses affect production, asset transactions, and financial fragility. It aims to build a credit-based foundation for an AI version of window guidance. The modeled loop is guidance conditions -> bank and borrower responses -> credit creation and spending -> production and balance sheets -> revised guidance. Credit is endogenous; neither a fixed pool of money nor full compliance with targets is assumed.

The credit-use distinction draws on Richard A. Werner's Quantity Theory of Credit (2012, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.irfa.2012.06.002). Werner's bank-accounting study (2014, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.irfa.2014.07.015) is a source for lending and deposit creation. Thermo-Credit state variables and AI guidance are proposed extensions, not results from those papers.

AI has two proposed roles: develop and test competing economic mechanisms, and compare guidance in a simulator using information available at the time. Institutions set objectives and permitted instruments. AI is not the final policy decision-maker.

Next deliverable: a stock-flow-consistent simulator with explicit lending, payment, repayment, and loss entries. Compare no guidance, fixed rules, transparent adaptive rules, and an AI controller under matched shocks. Test weak compliance, funding substitution, and behavioral misspecification with separate tuning and evaluation conditions. The simulator and AI controller are planned, not implemented results. Simulation gains would remain assumption-conditioned, not evidence of real-world policy effectiveness.

Primary links:

- English research program: https://www.toppymicros.com/Economy_AI_ERA.html
- Japanese research program: https://www.toppymicros.com/Economy_AI_ERA_ja.html
- Model and evaluation plan: https://github.com/ToppyMicroServices/2025_11_Thermo_Credit/blob/main/docs/mai_research_program.md

## RFC education

The site provides English and Japanese RFC learning guides and browser-based quizzes. They are educational utilities, not certifications.

The Agent-to-Agent design map separates:

1. Meaning, representation, discovery, and Agent Cards
2. Authentication, authorization, delegation, and sender-constrained tokens
3. Channel binding, signatures, and attestation
4. Transport, streaming, and versioning
5. Design review, threat modeling, and privacy

The map distinguishes current A2A references, background standards, references from a related session-bound identity draft, general design guidance, and RFCs for which quizzes are available. Adjacent security work is not presented as A2A core protocol text.

Primary links:

- English guide and quiz hub: https://www.toppymicros.com/education/rfc_quizzes.html
- Japanese guide and quiz hub: https://www.toppymicros.com/education/rfc_quizzes_ja.html

## Security, privacy, and legal context

### Coordinated vulnerability disclosure

The security policy covers public services under `toppymicros.com` and public repositories under the ToppyMicroServices GitHub organization. It asks reporters to use good-faith, low-impact testing, clear reproduction steps, and explicit scope.

Use the current policy page for reporting routes, scope, timelines, severity handling, and safe-harbor terms:

https://www.toppymicros.com/security-policy.html

### Privacy

The privacy policy describes the controller, processed data, analytics, GDPR legal bases, retention, recipients and transfers, data-subject rights, security, and policy changes.

Current policy:

https://www.toppymicros.com/privacy-policy.html

### Terms and legal notice

The site provides company information, public proof artifacts, educational material, and product pages. Unless a separate written agreement says otherwise, site content is informational and does not create a client relationship.

Current terms:

https://www.toppymicros.com/terms-legal-notice.html

## Source hierarchy

When sources differ, use this order:

1. A page or repository explicitly identified as the source of truth
2. The current product, policy, or project page
3. This full-site context summary
4. The short `llms.txt` navigation file

For release status, implementation details, and exact technical claims, consult the linked repository and its current tagged artifacts. For legal, privacy, and security-reporting questions, consult the current policy pages.
